claim: Exact deterministic fixed-sweep complete-state transport tradeoff; polynomial fingerprint escape under bounded error.
proof: For each r>=4, on the promised paired-map encoding, UNSAT iff the maps are identical; diagonal set has r! possibilities. Consider one locally moving read-only input head and an arbitrary deterministic mutable work state, with no other source access, a publicly fixed schedule of q full alternating monotone sweeps, and no uncharged timing or external transcript channel. At each fixed middle cut the parties holding the two input halves simulate their own intervals and transfer the complete mutable state at every crossing (including all control, storage, head positions and externally retained registers). If two distinct diagonals give identical state transcripts at that cut, deterministic splicing forces the same UNSAT answer on their SAT crossed hybrid. Thus the q state transcripts are injective on r! possibilities. For fixed-size s-bit complete state codes, 2^(qs)>=r!, so qs>=log2(r!). For variable-length state, take a prefix-free complete encoding at each cut, and write S(t) for its bit length. Concatenation of q prefix-free encodings is prefix-free; entropy gives average total code length across each cut >=log2(r!). Sum over D cuts; each crossing is a distinct time event, so E[CM_state]>=D log2(r!) and some diagonal attains it. This excludes read-only input storage from S but includes control, all state encoding overhead and metadata. For a fixed number of ordinary contiguous work tapes, codes use O(S_work+1) bits at a cut (input position and sweep index public; work-head indices encoded in O(log(S_work+1))). Consequently E[CM_work+control]=Omega(D log2(r!)). No claim for RAM sparse state omitting addresses, or free remote reads, adaptive schedule carrying unmetered timing, or unrestricted P vs NP. For r=256, D=18287, q=1 requires at least 1684 complete state bits; q=4 requires at least 421. This is a model-specific lower bound, not minimum runtime. A bounded-error fingerprint counteralgorithm uses a prime p>4r, evaluates the difference of the two degree-(r-1) map polynomials at a uniformly sampled field point, and compares. On every diagonal always equal; on each off-diagonal, at most r-1 roots so false-UNSAT probability <1/4. Work state O(log r) bits after charged prime acquisition (trial division over [4r,8r] polynomial, by Bertrand); one full read-only pass with exact modular Horner updates O(N polylog N) bit time after prime setup. Not an exact decision procedure. Deterministic exact alternative evaluates r distinct points in r scans, because polynomial degree<r, O(log r) state, polynomial aggregate work. Direct random access comparison uses O(N) bit probes, O(N log N) address traffic; balanced XOR/OR depth O(log N). Full encoding and permutation authentication separate and polynomial, fingerprint stream bound only for promised valid inputs. One-tape original crossing-state lower bound Omega(N^2) time and input-inclusive CM Omega(N^3) remains scoped; our read-only sweep theorem extends to charged workspace CM without input storage, not arbitrary global access.
model: PERM-TRANSPORT-BITSTRING-v1; logical ASCII bits, SHA on serialized ASCII
scope: All family parameters for symbolic proof, sampled/exhaustive controls as logged; no independent mathematical peer review.
